opened: October 31th, 1985 Temporarily Closed: November 12th, 1995 - April 7th, 1999 Re-Opened: April 8th, 1999
bio: The Adelaide Parklands is home to one of the most renowned street circuits in the world, the Adelaide Street Circuit and its jewel event, the Adelaide 500. Famous and talented drivers battle door to door at this legendary 2 mile street circuit through the hustle and bustle of downtown Adelaide and its tight, twisty turns that still attracts well over 200,000 people.

Portugal's most prestigious racetrack, Portimão has been a fan favorite to many road racing enthusiasts since 2008. The varying challenges of its turns between speed and tightness gives the track a flow that defines its character. To this day, Portimão's capacity of 100,000 people make it a true spectacle of a racetrack.

Welcome to sunny California and Next Gen in California. It’s going to be rainy weather for racing today. The Next Gen in California was located just east of Los Angeles on the site of an old steel mill. The wide, two mile long D-Shaped oval provides both driver and spectator with a great view of the largest attended sporting event in the state.

location: Scarperia e San Piero, Tuscany, Italy
bio: In the Apennines, Mugello remains today as one of Italy's favorite circuits. The well-known track combines high-speed straightaways with chicanes and hairpins to make it a fun and twisty complex. Ever since 1974, this three and a quarter mile road course remains a favorite to many people around the world making Mugello "The Beautiful Track in the Mountains."

wiki_title: Autodromo Internazionale Enzo e Dino Ferrari
bio: Located approximately 35 kilometers southeast of Bologna, the historic Circuit Enzo e Dino Ferrari combines short and medium speed straights with a challenging mix of slow turns and varying speed chicanes. Despite numerous revisions in order to improve safety, this circuit renamed in honor of the late Dino Ferrari remains one of Formula One’s classics.

Located just a few kilometers to the north of Milan, the legendary Monza Circuit combines long straights with a mixture of chicanes, fast sweeping, and 90 degree turns. The dedicated motorsports facility is the spiritual home of Italian Motor Racing and a cathedral for Ferrari and their fanatical fans, the Tifosi.

location: Mexico City, Mexico City District, Mexico
types: Mile Traditional Oval, Road Course, Roval
bio: Known for the famous Rodriguez brothers that raced here and its famous landmarks like the Magdalena Mixhuca Sports Complex and the Foro Sol Stadium, Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez has drawn huge crowds from multiple series from F1 to NASCAR and even the former CART and Champ Car series. To this day, the venue can put on a show with its high altitude of just over 7,000 feet giving the cars more speed leading to more excitement for the fans.

location: Sao Paulo, State of Sao Paulo, Brazil
bio: Located within the southern suburbs of Sao Paulo, the bumpy Interlagos circuit consists of two very distinct sections. The fast outer section combines two very long straights with fast sweeping turns whilst the technical infield contains some very slow corners that demand absolute precision and leave no room for driver error.

Located east of Birmingham, Alabama, Barber Motorsports Park is a fantastic race and test track for anyone to use. Its 2.38 mile road course and its 16 turns give drivers challenges as they travel down the track. Used by Skip Barber to test their Formula 2000 cars, this circuit loves races whenever they come to town.

Located in Kent, the Brands Hatch Circuit is a rather unique track. Located not far from Britain’s vast motorways, the track contains some of the trickiest turns in automotive racing. 9 turns in all and a gruesome track makes Brands Hatch a fantastic place to visit.

owner: Speedway Motorsports, Inc. Type: Short-Track Traditional Bullring Oval
bio: Are you ready for intensity on wheels? Welcome to Bristol Motor Speedway! Bristol’s 26 degree banked concrete bullring provides some of the sports most exciting fender-banging racing. 146,000 thousand permanent seats and a half mile layout guarantees the crowd is loud and hungry for action.

owner: Speedway Motorsports, Inc. Type: Dirt Short-Track Traditional Bullring Oval
bio: Are you ready for dirt racing on wheels? Welcome to Bristol Motor Speedway! Bristol's 26 degree banked dirt bullring provides dirt racing fans some of the most exciting fender-banging racing. 146,000 thousand permanent seats and a half mile layout guarantees the crowd is loud and hungry for action.

owner: Speedway Motorsports, Inc. Type: Dirt Short-Track Traditional Bullring Oval
bio: Are you ready for dirt racing on wheels? Welcome to Bristol Motor Speedway! Bristol's 26 degree banked dirt bullring provides dirt racing fans some of the most exciting fender-banging racing. 146,000 thousand permanent seats and a half mile layout guarantees the crowd is loud and hungry for action.

The scenic Lincolnshire Wolds National Landscape plays host to a racing circuit that has been around for nearly a whole century. That circuit is the Cadwell Park Circuit and with its varying types of turns and decent length straightaways, a track that is normally used for bike racing can also be a friend to even racecars on any given day.

The Canadian Tire Motorsport Park located in Bowmanville, Ontario is one of the true classic road courses. The track is not very complex but many racing series have unlocked the secret emerald to lure fans to the stands. With 10 turns and just under two and a half miles, Canadian Tire reminds drivers how challenging a track can be with minimal turns.

Hello and welcome to the Charlotte Motor Speedway at Concord. Even though it was built more than four decades ago, drivers still love to race at this mile and a half quad oval. If Daytona is the pinnacle of NASCAR Racing, then Charlotte has to be just a bumper behind. Fans flock to the largest sports facility in the southeast, home track to many of NASCAR’s teams.

owner: Chicago Department of Transportation Type: Street Circuit
bio: Welcome to the newest street course on the circuit located in downtown Chicago. This track that is just over 2 miles in length takes drivers through a breathtaking view of Chicago's Grant Park right alongside Lake Michigan and Lakeshore Drive. Not a very complex and tricky track by any means but this track's 90 degree turns definitely make up for its unique shape.

seating: 47,000 Nickname: The Magnificent Mile and a Half
bio: Hello and welcome to the Chicagoland Speedway. Chicagoland’s unique arched backstretch makes it worthy to all drivers and fans. Located on the outskirts of Joliet, action here never sleeps as the cars roar around this one and a half mile tri-oval. Opened less than two decades ago, this unique speedway is becoming one of the drivers' favorite racetracks.

Located just a few kilometers to the north of Barcelona, the superb Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya combines medium speed straights with an interesting selection of slow, medium, and high speed turns. This dedicated motorsports facility is a good example of modern circuit design and is highly rated by most of the teams, both as a race and testing venue.

Located in southern France in the Occitania region, Circuit de Lédenon is a twisty 2 mile complex with challenging corners and fast straights leading to great road racing competition. For drivers they will have to focus as much as they can at Lédenon as this track will make them twist and turn for nearly 15 turns before coming back to the front straight.

Located just a few kilometers south of Nevers, the Magny-Cours circuit combines several short straights with an interesting selection of slow to medium speed turns, hairpins, and chicanes. Like the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, Magny-Cours is a modern facility built specifically for motor racing.

Located approximately 50 kilometers north of Liege near the town of Spa, the exhilarating Spa-Francorchamps circuit comes with a challenging mix of fast turns and chicanes. Winding its way among the forests and the foothills of the Ardennes Mountains, Spa-Francorchamps also has the longest lap of all the current Formula 1 circuits.

location: Le Mans, Pays de la Loire, France
owner: Automobile Club de I'Quest Ville du Mans
bio: The Circuit des 24 Heures du Mans is France’s pride and joy when it comes to race tracks. The 24 hour race held here remains traditional and draws in crowds, drivers, teams, spectators, and more from around the world to watch Hypercar and GTE car action here at Le Mans. With over 40 racecars during the 24 hour race, Le Mans is by no means a true classic circuit through and through.

Located on the Île Notre-Dame just minutes away from Downtown Montreal, the Circuit Gilles-Villeneuve combines short straights with an uninspiring selection of slow to medium speed chicanes and one hairpin. Despite being a dedicated motorsports facility, the barriers around Circuit Gilles-Villeneuve are very close to the track, giving the circuit a distinctly street feel.

One of the newest road courses in America, COTA features the F1 American Grand Prix and boasts 20 unique, challenging turns. This particular track can wear down a driver, but the crowds love the action at this tight and twisty complex. With state-of-the-art facilities that surrounds the track on all sides, COTA remains as one of the gems in the racing world.

difficulty: Advanced Former Names: Circuit van Zandvoort (1948 - 1988) Circuit Park Zandvoort (1989 - 2016) Circuit Zandvoort (2017 - 2019) CM.com Circuit Zandvoort (2020 - 2024)
bio: Located on the shores of the coast of the Netherlands, Mascot Circuit Zandvoort is a circuit where road course racing in Europe never dwindles. The challenging circuit has banking and tight turns to make the drivers really earn their stripes. Of all the tracks in the Netherlands, Zandvoort is truly the “Diamond Of The Coast”.

Home of DTM and no stranger to any road racing series, Circuit Zolder is always a nice stop on the schedule to experience more variety of European Racing Circuits. Many people agree that Zolder is a true racing spectacle that contains multiple turns and tight corners which makes this track a motorsports haven.

location: Jerez de la Frontera, Andalusia, Spain
seating: 125,000 Type: Road Course Owners: City of Jerez and the Andalusian Regional Government
bio: Hello and welcome to one of Spain's most well known racetracks, the Circuito de Jerez - Ángel Nieto. This pristine track located in the outskirts of Jerez in Andalusia has been a favorite for both racecars and motorbikes for over 30 years. With challenging turns and fast straightaways, this premier track in Europe pays tribute to Ángel Nieto to this day.

Located in the town of Los Arcos, the Circuito de Navarra is a fairly young circuit consisting of a twisting layout with slow and medium speed turns and a few long straightaways. Being the only circuit in the entire autonomous community of Navarre, the Circuito de Navarra has done well with itself being a fan favorite to many people around the world.

Located not far from the famous Charlotte Motor Speedway, the Concord Speedway was a half-mile triangle that packed lots of action. The drivers that headed to this track stunned the crowds at the skills they possessed. Featuring tight turns, this tri-oval was a whole other beast that definitely needed taming.

Welcome to NASCAR’s oldest superspeedway, Darlington Raceway in South Carolina. The “Lady in Black”, “The Grand Daddy Of Them All”, call it what you will, The Darlington is always one thing, a challenge. This unique mile and a third egg-shaped oval has well earned the nickname “The Track Too Tough To Tame.”

Welcome to the Sunshine State and the birthplace of NASCAR, Daytona Beach, Florida. Since 1959, a drivers career can be made or broken at Daytona International Speedway. The two and a half mile tri-oval has served as a proving ground for some of the greatest names in racing. 31 degrees of banking in the turns, and incredible speeds on the straightaways, have led to the inclusion of restrictor plates here. Aerodynamic drafting has become a must have skill in order to stay with the pack and master Daytona.

wiki_title: Detroit Grand Prix at Belle Isle
bio: Commonly known as the Detroit Grand Prix, the Detroit Grand Prix at Belle Isle was one of the most prestigious road courses in all of America. Its tight 14 turns of many 90 degree angles has evolved this track from a easy Sunday drive to a difficult Monday morning Rush Hour. No matter how heavy the traffic, drivers always find a way to keep this track under any green flag conditions.

owner: MotorSport Vision Nickname: The Heart of British Motorsport
bio: Welcome to Donington Park, the heart of British motorsport located in Leicestershire, England. With over 2 miles in length and over 10 turns, Donington has become one of the world's most favorite racetracks. Of all the British tracks within the United Kingdom, Donington has been home to fantastic racing action for many years.

owner: Speedway Motorsports, Inc. Type: Mile Traditional Oval
bio: Hello and welcome to the Dover Motor Speedway in Delaware’s capital. This mile long concrete oval houses some of the most intense racing in NASCAR today. Some of the biggest crowds on the eastern seaboard flock to the “Monster Mile” to see the best drivers in the world battle door to door.

Welcome to Hampton, Georgia, home of the EchoPark Speedway. This ultra-modern multi-purpose venue has become one of the fastest tracks on the NASCAR circuit. 24 to 28 degree banking around the mile and a half quad oval serves as a slick, super competitive racetrack.

Both by geography and history, Eldora Speedway stands at the epicenter of dirt track racing. Situated in what was once an Ohio cornfield, the half-mile clay oval lies in the very heart of the Midwest racing scene. Hosting some of the biggest events on the calendar to date, Eldora rightly bills itself as “The World’s Greatest Dirt Track.”

Hello and welcome to the Fairbury American Legion Speedway. This fast, thrilling, quarter-mile dirt track keeps drivers on the steering wheel and the pedals. With a 6,600 seating capacity and roaring competition, you can bet that the Fairbury American Legion Speedway is no laughing matter.

wiki_title: I-55 Federated Auto Parts Raceway Park
bio: Welcome to "The Ironman Track" herself, the I-55 Federated Auto Parts Raceway Park. This high speed, 1/3 mile dirt track makes drivers of all ages rip up the track for some good fun. This facility with banking up to 19 degrees and being home to the Ironman 55 has turned it into one of dirt racing’s fastest tracks.

seating: 7,500 Nickname: America's Favorite Home Track Owners: Tim Bryant and Randy Bryant
bio: A half mile, paved oval opened in 1953, Five Flags Speedway takes its name from its proximity to Pensacola, Florida, known as the “City of Five Flags.” The race track is one of the fastest short tracks in America, thanks to its 15 degree banking and its wide turns that give the track a nearly circular configuration.

One of Japan's most challenging circuits, Fuji International Speedway has evolved from a high-speed racetrack into a twisty, technical complex. Featuring tough corners and its long front straightaway, the action that is showcased at Fuji lives long even after over 50 years of existence that makes this track a living legend to this day.

Welcome to the Tar Heel State and the Hickory Motor Speedway, known as The Birthplace of the NASCAR Stars. This small but exciting 0.363 mile track contains some of the most exciting fender-banging short track racing there is to date. While the track itself has long said goodbye to its former glory years, it can still give the crowds plenty of action.

bio: Located near the historic city of Heidelberg, the Hockenheimring Baden-Württemberg consists of three short straights and a really diverse mixture of fast, medium, and slow turns including a hairpin. This circuit was also originally built as a test track for Mercedes-Benz cars. The claustrophobic stadium section is the only feature that designer Hermann Tilke has left intact from the Hockenheim circuit as used in recent years.

Welcome to gorgeous south Florida and the Homestead-Miami Speedway. Known today as The Championship Track and one of the favorites on the NASCAR circuit, Homestead draws huge crowds with its distinctive blend of length at a mile and a half and 20 degrees of banking. This leads to real driving exhibitions for happy fans.

owner: Hungaroring Sport Zrt Type: Road Course
seating: 70,000 Former Names: Hungaroring (1986 - 1994, 2005 - Present), Hungaroring RT (1995 - 2004)
bio: Located just a few kilometers from Budapest, the Hungaroring combines just one straight of note with a complex selection of slow to medium speed turns. Opinions on this circuit are very much divided but whether you love or hate the venue, it appears to have a long term future in the F1 calendar being the only race hosted by a country from the former Eastern Bloc.

Not far from Sioux Falls, the Huset's Speedway is one of the top visited dirt ovals on the World of Outlaws circuit today and its low banking gives drivers a real challenge. Located near the tri-point of the state borders of South Dakota, Minnesota, and Iowa, fans come here to get down and dirty for some classic racing action.

Hello and welcome to the Indianapolis Motor Speedway. Known as “The Brickyard”, Indy is home to the world famous Indy 500, the biggest and largest motorsports race around the world. Considered relatively flat by American standards, the two and a half mile rectangular oval has been full of automotive excitement for over a century.

track_type: Road Course; Oval; Roval; Short Track
bio: Welcome to Newton, Iowa, home to the Iowa Speedway. This high-speed short-track features a 7/8ths mile oval. With a D-Shaped oval patterned after Richmond Raceway and with 14 degrees of banking in the turns, Iowa Speedway makes the fans and drivers here cheer loud and hard for “The Track Out in The Plains.”

Welcome to high-speed endurance that’s known to all drivers as the iRacing Superspeedway. This 36 degree banked, 3 mile superspeedway isn’t like any ordinary superspeedway. Instead of being a tri-oval superspeedway type, this track is a traditional oval shape and its length makes it a hyperspeedway which makes it rather unique. The restrictor plates have been taken off at this track to see how fast any racecar in the world can really go. ​

owner: Lindom Properties, Arcadia Former Names: Irwindale Speedway (1999 – 2007) Toyota Speedway at Irwindale (2008 – 2011) Irwindale Event Center (2012 - 2017)
types: Short-Track Traditional Oval, Short-Track Egg-Shaped Oval, Figure-Eight
bio: Heir to the proud tradition of short-track racing, the Irwindale Event Center opened in 1999 and for a quarter of a century, it hosted a variety of local and regional racing series. While it harks back to its old traditions of short-track racing, Irwindale was a modern-filled venue filled with amenities for drivers, crews, fans, and even sponsors as well.

It’s a perfect day for racing at Kansas Speedway in Kansas City, Kansas. This brand new state-of-the-art facility has brought NASCAR to the heartland. Although the tri-oval track design is not unique to Kansas, the slight difference in the banking makes this track truly different.

Welcome to the Kentucky Speedway. Located in the Bluegrass State, Kentucky Speedway is located on 850 acres of land near Sparta, Kentucky. Its one and a half mile tri-oval design, featuring a 1,600 hundred foot long backstretch and turns banked at 17 degrees, makes Kentucky no walk in the park even to NASCAR aficionados. ==

Welcome to the Kentucky Speedway. Located in the Bluegrass State, Kentucky Speedway is located on 850 acres of land near Sparta, Kentucky. Its one and a half mile tri-oval design, featuring a 1,600 hundred foot long backstretch and turns banked at 17 degrees, makes Kentucky no walk in the park even to NASCAR aficionados.

wiki_title: Bakersfield Speedway at Kevin Harvick's Kern Raceway
bio: Just located nearby to its bigger paved brother, Bakersfield Speedway at Kevin Harvick's Kern Raceway is a fun dirt oval for many racers and fans alike. While its small layout guarantees some tight fender banging style racing and plenty of cars in traffic, this small dirt oval can surely entertain crowds of all ages.

Located along the I-5 corridor near Bakersfield, Kevin Harvick's Kern Raceway is a fantastic half mile oval that features plenty of great racing action and competition. While the track itself is a replacement for Mesa Marin Raceway, both of its oval and dirt oval tracks have plenty of cheering crowds that are hungry for roaring racecars on any raceday.

track_type: Road Course; Oval; Roval; Short Track
types: Short-Track Scalene Triangular Oval, Road Course, Roval
bio: A racetrack that is fun, action, surprises, and more, the Knockhill Racing Circuit is one of the crown racing circuit jewels in the United Kingdom, Located in Scotland, this action packed track with an easy flow of turns and great competition keeps the crowds hungry for more.

difficulty: Novice Owners: State of California, Los Angeles County, and City of Los Angeles
bio: A stadium that has been around for nearly a whole century, welcome to the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum Raceway in downtown Los Angeles. A short quarter mile racetrack gives the crowd plenty of fender banging racing to enjoy. This track's minimal banking gives the drivers a new challenge while also having to battle with other drivers and this track's super tight turns.

Welcome to the Langley Speedway in Hampton, Virginia. Immediately adjacent to NASA’s Langley Research Center, the oval has been the launching pad for many NASCAR careers and was the site of nine NASCAR Grand National races. With a length of under 4/10ths of a mile, this track can be tricky to master with under 10 degrees of banking in the turns.

Welcome to the Lanier Speedway in Braselton, Georgia just across the street from Road Atlanta. The Lanier Speedway is one of the toughest and most brutal short tracks to ever exist in the racing world. With a length of 3/8ths of a mile and 11 degrees of banking in the turns, the drivers practice hard and long since this track does not give you the victory quite so easily.

Returning back to its dirt former glory, the Lanier Speedway Dirt Configuration challenges both car and machine alike. With 11 degrees in its 4 turns and 5 degrees on the straightaways, the fatigue and the skills of the drivers will be pushed to their limits. The hundreds of dealt horsepower on this tiny, dirt oval in Northern Georgia will be no Sunday Drive for the entire field.

Welcome to the glamorous Las Vegas Motor Speedway in Las Vegas, Nevada. Home to casino’s and fancy hotels, this one and a half mile tri-oval makes “The Diamond in the Desert” a well deserved racetrack home to the most popular tourist spot in the state.

owner: Ted Tomson Track Map ----> Type: Dirt Short-Track D-Shaped Oval
bio: Welcome one and all to the Lernerville Speedway. Lernerville is all about high-speed, fast-paced action. Located in Sarver, Pennsylvania, this D-shaped oval is one of the many examples of classic short-track dirt racing. With stiff competition and high banking, this speedway takes no prisoners.

Welcome to the Limaland Motorsports Park in Elida, Ohio. This fast 3/10ths mile oval gives thrill and speeds like no other short-track dirt oval. With the fans coming from all over the area to watch the drivers put on a spectacular show, its still known today as Ohio’s “1/4 Mile of Thunder.”

Nestled within the Berkshire Mountains in the northwest corner of Connecticut, Lime Rock Park is as picturesque for visitors as it is challenging for drivers. At a relatively short one and a half miles in length, fans flock from around the eastern seaboard to see great competition at this fantastic circuit.

wiki_title: Acura Grand Prix of Long Beach
bio: From the streets of Los Angeles, welcome to Long Beach. Long Beach is a two mile street circuit with 11 turns winding through the streets of the city's coastline. The location gives the track a downtown feel and with visits from multiple racing series, drivers want to come here to see if they can be victorious in the Golden State.

owner: National Hot Rod Association Nickname: America's Great Race Place
bio: The Lucas Oil Indianapolis Raceway Park is one of America’s premier multiple racing facilities. The track is home to a quarter mile drag strip and its nearly 7/10th mile oval configuration. Finding the fastest line around here has been a daunting challenge to the drivers themselves while still keeping their machine in pristine condition.

Hello and welcome to the Lucas Oil Speedway in the heart of the Ozark Highlands. With tight corners but thrilling action giving fans plenty of action on raceday gives this track the nickname, the diamond of dirt tracks.

Hello and welcome to a piece of racing history, the Martinsville Speedway in south central Virginia. Martinsville was opened before NASCAR was even founded. It’s one of the sports original tracks. It’s paperclip shaped half-mile has grown from a dusty pioneer to a beautiful racing facility with personality and unique challenges every time.

The Miami International Autodrome is one of America's newest racetracks for grand prix racing and the prowess nature of the facility shows. The modern facilities and grandstands, along with its contemporary look and feel is definitely fitting for America's Monaco. While the racing itself is home to Formula 1's Miami Grand Prix, the track's overall flat nature and tight and twisty complex nature gives drivers a whole new challenge for them to master.

This is the Michigan International Speedway, home to the automobile industry and some great competition. If you like three and four wide racing, then Michigan’s your track. This two mile d-shaped oval allows for great action with its high banks and wide surface. Located just outside the Motor City, drivers are always hoping to put on a great show for the auto industry here.

track_type: Road Course; Oval; Roval; Short Track
types: Short-Track Traditional Oval, Road Course, Roval
bio: Welcome to the Mid-Ohio Sports Car Course in Lexington, Ohio. One of the newest road courses on the NASCAR circuit, competition reigns king here. The full two and a quarter mile road course combines tricky turns and high speeds and with up to 8 degrees of banking in the turns, it has become a classic circuit in all of motorsports.

Hello and welcome to Misano, one of Italy's top racetracks. Hosting many series to this day, Misano features long straights with chicanes and challenging turns which makes this track a true challenge to any hardened veteran racer. Ever since 1972, this track has always been a stones throw away from the Adriatic Sea making The Adriatic Gem all the more exquisite that pays tribute to the late, great Marco Simoncelli.

types: Intermediate Egg-Shaped Oval, Road Course, Roval
bio: Welcome to Mobility Resort Motegi. An air of anticipation and excitement fills the track as both the cars and stars are set to entertain race fans of all ages. The racetrack is located 60 miles northeast of Tokyo and 100 miles due east of Nagano, home of the 1998 Winter Olympics. This is an exciting track with plenty of room on the straights leading to close, action packed, side-by-side racing.

Welcome to the MotorLand Aragón, Aragón's prestigious road racing circuit. Home to a wide variety of racing ranging from Formula 4's and Touring Cars to the European Le Mans Series and even Motorbikes makes this track both fun and technical that are contained in this tracks challenging turns.

difficulty: Clubman Owners: Thomas Voss and Ralph Bohnhorst
bio: Located in Saxony-Anhalt, Oschersleben is Germany's third permanent motor racing circuit after the Nurburgring and the Hockenheimring. Featuring a multitude of corners, this track has become fast but also tricky to master. With spectator areas above the track, it provides many viewing angles across most of the circuit.

Nestled in Bathurst, Mount Panorama gives fans the thrill of high speeds and tight turns in one package. With over 20 turns, this track is not easy to tame to any pro driver. Known as “The Mountain”, this daunting, dangerous circuit contains high elevation changes and fierce competition that gives "The Mountain" its name.

location: Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, United States
bio: Since opening in 1958 and through its transition to pavement in 1974 until its closure in 2020, Myrtle Beach Speedway was not only the scene of great weekly action but, a springboard for stock car racing royalty. The half-mile D-shaped oval is not anything new to the oval racing world but remains quite an adversary to short-track racing. With the track closed since August 2020, this South Carolina racetrack will definitely be missed.

owner: Tennessee State Fairgrounds Type: Short-Track Traditional Oval
bio: Welcome to the oldest continually operating track, the Nashville Fairgrounds Speedway in Nashville, Tennessee. Operating since 1904, this 3/5th's mile speedway has been thrilling fans and hosting great competition for well over 100 years. As a matter of fact, this racetrack is older than the famed Indianapolis Motor Speedway by only 5 years and has had 9 name changes, more than any other track in the world today.

owner: Speedway Motorsports, Inc. Type: Intermediate Tri-Oval
bio: Hello and welcome to the Music City and the Nashville Superspeedway. Ever since its opening in 2001, this track has definitely become one of the many oval favorites and still shines on today. With banking ranging from 3 to 14 degrees, this track can still pack a lot of fun for many drivers to please as many spectating fans as possible.

owner: Speedway Motorsports, Inc. Nickname: The Magic Mile
types: Mile Traditional Oval, Road Course, Roval
bio: Hello and welcome to Loudon, New Hampshire. At a distance of just over a mile, this squared-off oval has seen some fantastic finishes in its history. Over 70,000 thousand people attend each race, coming from nearby Boston, Providence, and all of New England, to see the action at New Hampshire Motor Speedway.

Located a few miles down the road from its more celebrated neighbor, New Smyrna Speedway is the place to be for hard-core racers during Speedweeks. The high-banked, half mile oval hosts from stock car racing to open wheel modified cars. Famous NASCAR drivers started their career here and the track has proven to be an increasingly popular test venue among NASCAR’s teams.

location: North Wilkesboro, North Carolina, United States Nationality: American
opened: May 18th, 1947 Temporarily Closed: January 1st, 1997, May 10th, 2011 Reopened: September 5th, 2010, August 2nd, 2022
bio: Welcome to the Appalachian mountains and the North Wilkesboro Speedway. This unique oval is truly one of the NASCAR classics and still is today. With a downhill front straightaway and an uphill back straightaway, no one can deny that the North Wilkesboro Speedway is one of NASCAR’s legendary racetracks.

The most fearsome of all racing tracks in the whole world, the Nürburgring Combined is over 14 miles long which features over 160 turns. The famous Karussell turn and the long straight at Döttinger Höhe is one of the highlights of this gruesome race track through the Eifel Mountains in Nurburg, Germany. With many turns here, fowling up results in a drivers race completely shot. Luck and skill are required to master this treacherous circuit known to all drivers around the world as the “Green Hell”.

Located approximately 60 kilometers northwest of Koblenz, the Nurburgring combines short straights with a challenging combination of slow, medium, and fast turns. Whilst the new Nurburgring pales into insignificance compared to the original Nordschleife Circuit, the fatalities of yester year more than justify today’s safety standards which render the old 13 mile loop redundant.

Located in the Eifel Mountains in Germany, the Nürburgring Nordschleife is one of the most gruesome race tracks in the world. Skill wins the race here as the track contains over 150 turns and some of the most dangerous corners on any racing circuit in the world. Drivers here must focus on all of these turns and put out their best effort to even put down a decent lap time. The hardest thing they will have to master is being consistent.

Nestled in the mountains of Japan, the Okayama International Circuit is one of the most popular race tracks. Many types of racecars come here to get the thrills of this two and one-thirds mile road course. With variable banking in the turns, one has to be patient in order to be the Senshi at Okayama.

Oran Park Raceway, now demolished, was a circuit like no other. With a crossover point that featured a bridge, the tracks 12 turns gave drivers new and exciting corners to get used to. Now part of a housing area, Oran Park Raceway always had a ton of superb racing action for both fans and spectators to enjoy.

The Home of the Super Modified herself, Oswego Speedway is a beautiful 5/8 mile racetrack with a beautiful location right along the Lake Ontario waterfront. Known to many drivers as "The Big O" and "The Steel Palace", drivers and fans love coming to this racetrack time and time again to experience its well-known cut throat competition and cheering fans.

It only happens a few days out of the year, Oswego Speedway's dirt configuration has now become a staple classic for dirt racing fans all over the globe ever since the closure and demolition of the Syracuse Mile. The SuperDIRT week as its known with the tracks usual 4 to 13 degrees of banking in the turns and 6 degrees on the straightaways makes this track quite an exciting place to be. Nearly 10,000 thousand dirt fans cheer loud and proud for their favorite drivers battling for every position during raceday.

In Little Budworth, a circuit known as Oulton Park still survives today. Opened in August of 1953, the race track features 17 challenging turns testing drivers skills and patience like never before. With a max length beyond two and a half miles, this track requires a whole new strategy and experience in order to conquer Oulton Park.

Maine is the northeastern most state of the United States and the 14,000 seat Oxford Plains Speedway is the biggest public facility in the Pine Tree State. Opened in 1950, the facility today features street stocks, legends cars, and more despite the tracks small circular shape. Even though it’s a tiny 3/8ths mile oval, drivers keep coming back to experience its dizzying thrill.

opened: March 21st, 1928 (road circuit), December 15th, 1952 (modern circuit) Temporarily Closed: 1940, 1965 - 1966, 1978 - 1987 Reopened: 1967, December 4th, 1988
bio: Located on Phillip Island south of Melbourne, the Phillip Island Grand Prix Circuit is home to over two and a half miles of intense road racing. With two tight hairpins and fierce opposition, this track does not play around. With beautiful cliff side edges and spectacular views of the water, this leaves this track in an unique beauty of its own.

Welcome to the valley of the sun and the Phoenix Raceway. This gem in the desert has been shining since 1964 with its unique design and beautiful surroundings, its earned its reputation as one of the top visits on the circuit.

Welcome to the infamous Pocono Raceway in Long Pond, Pennsylvania. This two and a half mile scalene triangular shaped superspeedway features three unique turns with different banking from six to fourteen degrees. With five and six wide racing possible, this track is rightfully known as the “Tricky Triangle.”

Hello and welcome to the Port Royal Speedway in the Susquehanna Valley in its namesake town in Pennsylvania. This fast half mile dirt oval known to all dirt oval drivers as The Speed Palace has definitely earned its nickname that plays host to fantastic racing and stiff competition.

Welcome to the Beaver State and the Portland International Raceway. Located within the downtown heart of Oregon's most populated city, Portland features fast straightaways and a short twisty complex that delivers a thrilling two miles full of experience and intense racing action like no other making it the premier road course in the pacific northwest.

Qualcomm Circuit is NASCAR's newest street circuit built on an active US Navy base near San Diego. The tight and fast sweeping corners here give this track quite a unique feel and character different from other street circuits. The track itself has an interesting scenery of aircraft carriers, fighter jet planes, plane hangars and more which gives The Q a challenge that both fans and drivers all enjoy.

owner: Dietrich Mateschitz Beteiligungs GmbH Type: Road Course
bio: Located near Knittelfeld in the foothills of the Styrian mountains, the Red Bull Ring combines three long straights with a flowing mix of fast sweeping and slower 90 degree turns. Built on the site of the historic Österreichring, this dedicated motorsports facility is another fine example of modern circuit design.

Whether under the lights or the bright sun of day, the Richmond Raceway is home to excitement. The “Action Track” as its known, combines the best of both worlds, superspeedway speeds and short-track action. At three quarters of a mile on length, it’s not unusual to witness tempers flaring at Richmond.

Located outside the picturesque village of Elkhart Lake, Road America resides. This racetrack is one of the worlds classic road-racing venues and has been hosting a variety of racecars both oval and road spec for over 60 years. At over four miles in length, Road America's challenging turns makes this track demanding even to the most experienced drivers.

Located in Braselton, Georgia, the Michelin Raceway Road Atlanta is the hub of the Panoz Motor Sports Group and the American Le Mans Series. With multiple turns, the Michelin Raceway Road Atlanta can decimate a car on raceday. Cars and bikes of all shapes and sizes visit Michelin Raceway Road Atlanta to see what this roller coaster of a race track has in store waiting for them.

opened: October 31st, 1965 Temporarily Closed: 2015 - November 17th, 2021 Reopened: November 18th, 2021
types: D-Shaped Mile Oval, Road Course, Roval
bio: Under beautiful Carolina blue skies, welcome to the Rockingham Speedway, also known as “The Rock.” This one mile oval has been thrilling fans for over 30 years with 22 degrees of banking and a “tough on tires” surface, you get fierce competition that gives “The Rock” its name.

location: Rakkestad, Ostfold, Norway •Length: 2.022 Miles (3.254 km) •Turns: 14 •Configurations: 1 •Pit Road Speed: 31 mph (50 kmh) •Price: Free •Track Map ----> Type: Road Course Nickname: Home of the Gatebil Festival
bio: In the most southern part of Norway, the Rudskogen Motorsenter is still around after over 30 years of existence. Featuring a 2 mile road course through Norwegian scenery and rock cuts, this track is definitely the pride and joy of Norwegian racing.

Within the state of Saxony, one of Europe's favorite road courses resides. Hello and welcome to one of Germany's most historic venues, the Sachsenring. Home to mainly MotoGP and DTM races, this twisting 2.281 mile racetrack welcomes road racing vehicles of all shapes and sizes as the drivers battle their way through this technical complex that always remains challenging to rookies and seasoned veterans.

Nestled within the bustling suburbs of Melbourne, welcome to the Sandown International Motor Raceway. This bustling 2 mile course is one of the most interesting courses to date combining long straights and some tight turns, which definitely earns this track the nickname "The Home of Horsepower".

Laid out on the runways of a former air base and the adjacent roadways, Sebring is the oldest permanent road-racing circuit in the United States. At over three and a half miles, it proves challenging to the drivers to this very day. With an oddly shaped track design and home to the 12 Hour Grand Prix of Endurance, Sebring is still a tough track to master.

wiki_title: Shell V-Power Motorsport Park at The Bend
bio: Located in Tailem Bend in the state of South Australia, The Bend is one of the world's twistiest tracks. If you like turn-mania, this is definitely the track for you. With many configurations ranging from about a mile to nearly 5 miles in length and total turn count as high as 35 turns, The Bend surely deserves its name home to Supercars, GT Racing, Touring Cars and more gives this track a flashy and fancy feel.

Located just outside Northampton, the fantastic Silverstone Circuit combines two fast straights, slow, medium, and high speed turns. Surrounded by the headquarters of the McLaren Team, this disused airfield in the heart of Formula 1’s so-called Silicon Valley often plays host to one of the most competitive races of the season.

owner: British Racing Drivers' Club Nickname: Home of British Motor Racing
bio: Located just outside Northampton, the fantastic Silverstone Circuit combines two fast straights, slow, medium, and high speed turns. Surrounded by the headquarters of the McLaren Team, this disused airfield in the heart of Formula 1’s so-called Silicon Valley often plays host to one of the most competitive races of the season.

Located in southern Wisconsin, the insane but fun Slinger Speedway whirls cars around with high speeds and great action. Not far from the Milwaukee Mile, this track that has been hosting local races since 1948 has been a star shining bright ever since with its steep 33 degrees of banking in the turns and straightaway banking between 6 and 11 degrees has made Slinger a true short track beast in its own right.

Welcome to the Snetterton Circuit in Norwich, Norfolk. Originally part of a Royal Air Force airfield, Snetterton hosts Open Wheel and Sports Cars to create some of the most incredible racing in all of European motorsports. With banking up to three degrees in the tracks’ 13 turns, Snetterton always puts on a great show even to people that do not care about racing.

Welcome to the famous Napa Valley of northern California. One of the few road courses on the NASCAR circuit and one of the best in the world, Sonoma Raceway is a beautiful two mile track with multiple turns, testing a drivers skill and patience to the ultimate. The true test for drivers is to try and keep their eyes off the scenery and on the competition at Sonoma.

A mecca for Virginian short-track racing for over half a century, South Boston Speedway today bills itself as “America’s Hometown Track.” With a length of just under half a mile, the oval features late models, legends, modifieds, and street stock cars so the fans are never disappointed when race day comes to the South Boston Speedway.

In a little more than two decades, Southern National Motorsports Park has earned a reputation as one of the premier short-tracks in the Carolinas. Opened in 1993, the 17 degree banked 4/10ths mile speedway became part of NASCAR’s Home Tracks program as a host to NASCAR’s Whelen Modified Series. The track may be short on length but, the action still reigns at this tight, impressive oval.

wiki_title: Firestone Grand Prix of St. Petersburg
bio: Welcome to St. Petersburg, Florida and its flagship grand prix race sponsored by Firestone. St. Pete is a spectacular 1.8 Mile street circuit weaving in and around the downtown St. Pete area. Home to the IndyCar season opener and more, this facility where a portion of it is on the airport has transformed The Sunshine Race that grew up from troubled times to become a beautiful premier motorsports destination.

seating: 10,000 Owners: Jack Arute III and Mark Arute
bio: Built in 1870 for horse racing before automobile racing, Stafford Speedway traces the Modified lineage back to the very beginning of this track and stock car racing. Not as flashy and fancy as the half miles that the Cup Cars go to today, but this busy oval can still put on a fantastic show full of action for the fans and intense competition for the drivers.

location: Summit Point, West Virginia, United States
difficulty: Rookie Former Names: Summit Point Raceway (1969 - 2003)
bio: With the hilly, but high-speed 2 miles of action, Summit Point Motorsports Park offers every challenge a road-racer could desire with tight turns and long straights. All settled in West Virginia’s countryside, it’s still a challenging circuit. The Summit Point Motorsports Park feels like a fast tour over country roads that gives great action for all to see.

Located approximately 70 kilometers southwest of Nagoya, the exciting Suzuka Circuit combines two medium speed straights with a technical arrangement including a hairpin as well as fast sweeping and 90 degree turns. Owned by Honda, Suzuka has a somewhat unique Figure of 8 layout causing the track to cross over itself.

Welcome to the worlds fastest speedway, Talladega Superspeedway in Alabama. Talladega is the biggest, fastest, and most competitive motorsports facility in the world. Speed says it all about this place. Its record breaking two and two-thirds mile tri-oval keeps drivers glued to Earth by virtual 33 degree banking. Freight trains of stock cars in the draft literally caused the Earth to rumble in Alabama.

Welcome to Fort Worth and the Texas Motor Speedway. With seating for over 130,000 thousand fans, this motorsports haven represents racing at its finest. Recently repaved, this quad-shaped oval with 20-degree banking has become one of NASCAR’s fastest tracks.

Welcome to Fort Worth and the Texas Motor Speedway. With seating for over 150,000 thousand fans, this motorsports haven represents racing at its finest. Recently repaved, this quad-shaped oval with 24-degree banking has become one of NASCAR’s fastest tracks.

wiki_title: The Bullring at Las Vegas Motor Speedway
bio: The Bullring at Las Vegas Motor Speedway is racing’s answer to truth in short track action. This little circuit is located a stone’s throw away from the mile and a half tri-oval that is Las Vegas Motor Speedway. With just under 10 degrees of banking, The Bullring is an asphalt oval that’s short on distance, but long on action with great short-track competition.

owner: Speedway Motorsports, Inc. Type: Dirt Short-Track Traditional Oval
bio: Fast, wild, and entertaining, The Dirt Track at Charlotte is one of dirt racing’s highest spectacles. If Eldora is the height of Dirt Oval racing, then The Dirt Track at Charlotte must be a fender behind. Just next door to the famous Charlotte Motor Speedway, this track brings crowds from many parts of the world to see drivers battle for the checkered flag.

Here we are at The Milwaukee Mile, the oldest speedway in the world with auto racing taking place here since 1903. The grandstands offer great views of the track and the one-mile course offers great driving for the competitors.

seating: 15,000 Owners: Donald Hoenig and D.R. Hoenig
bio: The terms “Thompson Speedway” and “New England Motorsports” are all but synonymous. The track that became known as the “Indy of the East” was born out of the calamitous hurricane that devastated much of New England in 1938. With the track alive today, this 5/8ths mile that opened in May of 1940 features stock car and open wheel racing like no other. It is a classic circuit for action to endure.

Located in the county of Hampshire, Thruxton Circuit is a well known circuit in the local area that it serves to racing fans both car and bike alike. With turns that are both flowing and sharp, this completely flat circuit with a few elevation changes here and there offer drivers a different kind of strategy and a challenge to go fast with no banking at all.

Tiny and compact, Tsukuba Circuit is one of the most popular road courses in the world. Even though it rarely hosts any major championships these days, Tsukuba is one of the most recognized circuits in all of Japan thanks to being well-known in popular video games. Known as the Home of Time Attack, year round popularity has always soared here.

A three-quarter mile, semi-banked oval, USA International once hosted a variety of races for a couple of racing series. Located in Lakeland, Florida, it combines long straights and tight turns into a thrilling race track. The track demands a tuned engine and a tough chassis to get around this tracks’ nasty bumps.

A dirt track in Florida to coexist with Volusia Speedway Park, USA International Speedway – Dirt is one of the most fantastic three-quarter mile dirt tracks there is. Even though the dirt cars are more comfortable on shorter dirt race tracks, the competition at USA – Dirt always remains a challenge even to the most experienced.

A motorsports lazarus, Virginia International Raceway is a race track that came back from the dead after been previously closed in 1974. With the circuit being over three miles long, this road course features elevation change between 350 and 500 feet. The track features multiple turns keeping drivers on their toes making them think twice when viewing the surroundings.

location: Watkins Glen, New York, United States
bio: Welcome to the finger lakes region of New York state and Watkins Glen International. This world famous road course leads drivers through a fast, two and a half mile, twisting, twelve turns. With banking ranging from 6 to 10 degrees in the corners and great elevation changes, one always has to be alert in order to conquer Watkins Glen.

Welcome to WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca, a classic North American road-racing circuit. This beautiful serpentine ribbon of pavement features the famous Corkscrew turn, the most feared corner in all of the Americas. With 11 turns and nestled in desert highlands, it’s no wonder why the WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca is an automotive gem to many that drive on this legendary circuit.

Welcome to the track in the Californian highlands, the Willow Springs Raceway, Willow Springs is a fantastic two and a half mile track with minimal turns and great elevation changes which leads to some great action from the drivers. Located between Los Angeles and Bakersfield, The Big Willow is a great place to race.

location: Benalla, Victoria, AustraliaLength: 1.261 to 1.864 Miles (2.029 to 3.00 km)
difficulty: Clubman Former Names: Winton Motor Racing Circuit (1961 - 1976) Winton Motor Raceway (1977 - 2000, 2004 - Present) Winton Raceway (2001 - 2003)
bio: Welcome to Australia's action track, the Winton Motor Raceway in Benalla, Victoria. This nearly 2 mile long circuit has been quite the entertainment center for a while in the state. With seating for 30,000 hungry fans and dynamic action, its no wonder why this place is nicknamed "The Nation's Action Track".

difficulty: Clubman Former Names: St. Louis International Raceway (1967 – 1988) Gateway International Raceway (1989 – 2011) Gateway Motorsports Park (2012 - 2018) World Wide Technology Raceway at Gateway (2019 - 2023)
bio: Located in the shadow of the Gateway Arch, the World Wide Technology Raceway lies in the midst of multiple interstate junctions. Once a road course, the track today is now an egg-shaped speedway. This unique track is a fan favorite to all and is literally no stranger with its 10 degrees of banking in the turns.

owner: The Bark River Lions Club Type: Offroad Truck Dirt Road Course
bio: Home to the annual bark river off-road rumble, the Bark River International Raceway is one of the highlights on any off-road truck series schedule. Featuring tight turns and some curved jumps, this track is definitely a challenging course for all drivers that come here. While this track has to share part of its spotlight with its fellow neighbor, the Crandon International Off-Road Raceway, its a spotlight both will share for many years to come.

Welcome to Wisconsin and the Cedar Lake Speedway. Fans from around the Midwest gather to see fun and action at this 3/8's mile dirt speedway. Known as “Wisconsin’s Fastest Piece Of Real Estate”, this tricky little track thrills everybody from young children to even the most diehard of fans.

location: Adirondack Mountains, New York, United States
bio: Located in the Adirondack Mountains of New York, the Centripetal Circuit is a large skid pad designed to test cars and their braking, acceleration, handling, and much more. It’s a perfectly flat, perfectly round, circular test track with lane markers placed concentrically every 11 yards or so. It truly is a hidden gem of automotive research and design even to the inexperienced.

wiki_title: NOS Energy Drink Chili Bowl Nationals
bio: Welcome to the meanest dirt oval in the country, the Chili Bowl in the heart of Oklahoma. This quarter mile indoor dirt oval has been thrilling fans and entertaining drivers since 1987. Its reputation as being called the “Super Bowl of Midget Racing” still lives on to this very day.

owner: Cliff Flannery Type: Offroad Truck Dirt Road Course
bio: Full of land rush excitement and fan surprise, Crandon International Off-Road Raceway in Crandon, Wisconsin provides Lucas Oil trucks with a lot of fender-banging racing. The track itself is full of daring short jumps and a few sharp corners that can definitely be a challenge to any hardcore off-road racer. A one and a half mile layout with 8 turns and variable banking makes The Big House a very known presence in the off-road racing world.

seating: 3,033 Pavement: 70 - 75% Dirt: 25 - 30% Joker Entry: Turn 1, Right-Hand
bio: Not far from its prestigious speedway, Daytona Rallycross and off-road circuit blends both asphalt and dirt racing to create racing like no other. Its 12 turns and its massive jump on the backstretch makes this track a stranger to inexperience rallycross drivers. At a length of just over three-quarters of a mile, Daytona Rallycross and Dirt Road gives drivers more than enough competition than what they can handle.

seating: 1,200 Type: Offroad Truck Dirt Road Course
bio: Located in the desert of Arizona, the Firebird Motorsports Park is one of the toughest offroad truck races in the United States. With banking in the turns up to 4 degrees and fast acceleration on the straightaways, the jumps and the action created here makes this track truly fun for both the fans and drivers.

seating: 21,135 Nickname: Sprint Car Capital of the World
bio: Sprint Car Capital of the World, the Knoxville Raceway is one of many dirt track favorites. Located in Knoxville, Iowa, the half mile dirt-clay oval is home to sprint cars and late models. The 7 degrees of banking in the turns make the cars tear up the track for some of the greatest racing in all of dirt competition.

It’s a tight dirt oval, but home to fantastic racing. Welcome to the Kokomo Speedway in Kokomo, Indiana. This quarter mile dirt-clay oval that opened in 1947 thrills both the drivers and the fans. With 10 degrees of banking in the turns and 4 degrees on the straightaways, Kokomo Speedway keeps drivers on their feet as they battle for the positions that lead to winning or losing.

Returning back to its dirt former glory, the Lanier Speedway Dirt Configuration challenges both car and machine alike. With 11 degrees in its 4 turns and 5 degrees on the straightaways, the fatigue and the skills of the drivers will be pushed to their limits. The hundreds of dealt horsepower on this tiny, dirt oval in Northern Georgia will be no Sunday Drive for the entire field.

One of Pennsylvania's most well-known racetracks, Lincoln Speedway sits in the heart of southern Pennsylvania's Pigeon Hills between the towns of York and Gettysburg. With a 3/8's mile layout and over 6,000 roaring fans, dirt racing at this track remains the highlight of southern Pennsylvania racing even after 50 years of racing.

location: Hell, Trøndelag, Norway •Length: 0.46 to 0.67 Miles (0.74 to 1.08 km) •Turns: 7 - 8 •Configurations: 5 •Pit Road Speed: 20 mph (32 kmh) to 35 mph (56 kmh) •Price: $11.95 USD •Track Map ----> Type: Rallycross Circuit Nickname: Hell
bio: The Lånkebanen is one of Scandinavia’s best known rallycross circuits while also featuring a few gravel sections. Located within the mountainous landscape that defines Norway in its majestic beauty, the Lånkebanen is one of rallycross’ best circuits to date.

This is the Michigan International Speedway, home to the automobile industry and some great competition. If you like three and four wide racing, then Michigan’s your track. This two mile d-shaped oval allows for great action with its high banks and wide surface. Located just outside the Motor City, drivers are always hoping to put on a great show for the auto industry here.

difficulty: Novice Nickname: North Carolina's Premier Dirt Track
bio: Just north of the famed Charlotte Motor Speedway, the Millbridge Speedway packs a lot of fun for its small size. While the banking in this track is quite minimal, that doesn't mean the competitors are any less fierce. Home to micro sprints and the like, this track is a fan favorite to the many locals that it serves within the state.

owner: Pacific Group Resorts Inc. Nickname: The Climb To The Clouds Former Names: Mt. Washington by the Auto Road (1861 - 1969) Mt. Washington Auto Road (1970 - 1993, 2002 - Present) Mt. Washington Auto Road at Great Glen (1994 - 2001)
bio: Hello and welcome to the climb to the clouds herself, the Mount Washington Auto Road. Ever since competition began here in 1904, this fierce 7.60 mile hillclimb has been one of the most trickiest tracks in the entire United States. Located in upstate New Hampshire, this tight and twisty complex with 138 turns in all makes sure that drivers pay attention at all times.

Located adjacent to a former US Army Air Corps fighter pilot training field, New Jersey Motorsports Park pays homage to its legacy by naming its featured circuit “The Thunderbolt.” It’s two and one quarter shaped layout features multiple turns that may throw drivers off their A-Game.

Welcome to the valley of the sun and the Phoenix Raceway. This gem in the desert has been shining since 1964 with its unique design and beautiful surroundings, its earned its reputation as one of the top visits on the circuit.

types: Scalene Triangular Superspeedway, Road Course, Roval

This two and a half mile scalene-triangular shaped superspeedway features three unique turns with different banking from six to fourteen degrees. With five and six wide racing possible, this track is rightfully known as the “Tricky Triangle.”

Welcome to Fort Worth and the Texas Motor Speedway. With seating for over 150,000 thousand fans, this motorsports haven represents racing at its finest. Recently repaved, this quad-shaped oval with 24-degree banking has become one of NASCAR’s fastest tracks.

A dirt track in Florida to coexist with Volusia Speedway Park, USA International Speedway – Dirt is one of the most fantastic three-quarter mile dirt tracks there is. Even though the dirt cars are more comfortable on shorter dirt race tracks, the competition at USA – Dirt always remains a challenge even to the most experienced.

Known as the “Fastest Dirt Half Mile in the World,” Volusia Speedway Park is a favorite stop on both the World of Outlaws and Super DIRTcar Series calendars. Located in Barberville, Florida, the track has undergone a variety of changes since 1968, but the racing has always stayed competitive to keep the fans’ hunger for action alive. With 10 degrees of banking in the turns, the track and its nickname sells for itself.

owner: Al Heinke Former Names: Weedsport Speedway (1955 - 1980, 2013 - Present) Cayuga County Fair Speedway (1981 - 2012)
bio: Hello and welcome to the Weedsport Speedway. At over five decades old, drivers that come to Weedsport still love to duke it out at this D-Shaped dirt oval. The 11 degrees of banking in the turns and the fast attainable speeds here makes this track go from a Sunday drive to a champion level. This has resulted in hundreds of fans cheering for their favorite driver.

seating: 10,000 Type: Offroad Truck Dirt Road Course
bio: In the dusty desert of Nevada not far from Reno, the Wild West Motorsports Park even after half a decade stands its ground. One of the more exhilarating Offroad Truck Dirt Road Courses within the Western United States, fans from around the area come to visit this action packed race track for some action packed racing featuring tight turns and tall jumps.

Hearkening back to a classic era in American racing, Williams Grove Speedway features history like no other dirt track on the circuit. The long straights and tight turns challenge the dirt drivers to a whole new level. Located just south of Mechanicsburg, Pennsylvania, this track has since become woven into the DNA of American racing as we know it today.
